scientific_question: Does the fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons surrounded by a severe reactive-astrocyte cuff that also contains nearby lymphocytes capture an inflammatory perineuronal niche with memory-decline signal beyond the current astrocyte-only panel?
rationale: Rounds 3-6 show that CA1 peripyramidal reactive astrocyte cuffing and reactive-cell hypertrophy are the strongest lead, while round 7 suggests additional astrocyte-only burden summaries are becoming redundant. The next logical test is to keep the same CA1 pyramidal niche but add one biologically distinct component: lymphocyte admixture. This asks whether a smaller inflammatory subset of the established reactive cuffs is more informative than broader cuff-count or area summaries and could either add orthogonal signal or replace a weaker cuff feature.
approach: Assign cells to CA1 using the annotation polygons after dividing polygon coordinates by 16. Identify CA1 Pyramidal Neuron cells, Reactive Astrocyte cells, and Lymphocyte cells from ClassificationNode labels. For each CA1 pyramidal neuron, count nearby Reactive Astrocytes and Lymphocytes within radius r using centroid-to-centroid distance in microns. Define an immune-admixed severe reactive cuff as a pyramidal neuron with at least 2 Reactive Astrocytes and at least 1 Lymphocyte within radius r. The donor-level biomarker is the fraction of all CA1 pyramidal neurons meeting that criterion.

variations.name: ca1_pyramidal_immune_admixed_reactive_cuff_fraction_r35um_ra2_ly1
variations.description: Baseline: fraction of CA1 pyramidal neurons with >=2 Reactive Astrocytes and >=1 Lymphocyte within 35 um.

variations.name: ca1_pyramidal_immune_admixed_reactive_cuff_fraction_r50um_ra2_ly1
variations.description: Local radius expansion: same definition but within 50 um to allow a slightly broader inflammatory cuff.

notes: Use centroids from SegmentationNode for neighbor search; convert pixel distances to microns using slide MPP if available from the paired SVS, otherwise use the cohort-typical ~0.503 um/pixel consistently. Keep the denominator as all CA1 pyramidal neurons so donors with zero lymphocytes score 0 rather than becoming missing. Return NaN only if CA1 pyramidal neurons are absent. Avoid contour-area calculations here; this is a pure spatial composition feature.
prompt_text:
# Candidate Proposer

You are proposing exactly one candidate biomarker round for an iterative
autoresearch loop.

This system is deliberately simple:

- there is one accepted biomarker panel so far
- each round proposes one new candidate biomarker family
- the worker may test a small local sweep within that candidate family
- the evaluator compares:
  - current accepted panel score
  - panel + candidate score
  - panel with one member replaced by the candidate
- the system then keeps the best reviewed panel only if it improves the train panel score

Your job is only to propose the next candidate.

You will receive a JSON payload containing:

- `program`: the research directive
- `data_summary`: dataset guide
- `accepted_panel`: the current accepted biomarker panel
- `recent_results`: recent keep/discard history from results.tsv
- `round_id`
- `candidate_type`: `seed` if the panel is empty, otherwise `candidate`

## Output

Return exactly one JSON object:

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "short stable slug",
  "scientific_question": "one sentence stating the candidate hypothesis",
  "rationale": "why this candidate is the right next test based on recent results",
  "approach": "how to compute the biomarker from the data",
  "variations": [
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_a",
      "description": "baseline or central parameterization"
    },
    {
      "name": "candidate_variant_b",
      "description": "one nearby local change"
    }
  ],
  "baseline_variation": "candidate_variant_a",
  "notes": "data access, coordinate, or implementation notes for the worker"
}
```

## Rules

- Propose exactly one candidate family per round.
- Keep the candidate biologically interpretable.
- If `candidate_type` is `seed`, propose the strongest plausible seed biomarker.
- If `candidate_type` is `candidate`, propose something that could improve the
  accepted panel either by adding new signal or by being a cleaner replacement
  for one weaker existing member.
- Prefer one local family sweep with 2-4 nearby variations, not a grab bag of
  unrelated ideas.
- Use recent results to avoid exact repetition.
- Make the local sweep explicit and small:
  - one radius change
  - one threshold change
  - one local operator change
  - or one biologically coherent gating change
- Do not talk about planners, branches, coordinators, or analyzers.
- Focus on one candidate that is easy to compute and easy to audit.

## Quality bar

A good proposal is:

- specific
- testable in one round
- mechanistically interpretable
- plausibly additive to the accepted panel
- not a vague restatement of the prior winner
